correctness.rationale: For all fields and n>=2, Sylvester ranks yield exactly every rank between max(0,r+s-n) and min(r,s), including every target matrix of that rank by GL-left/right invariance. Nonidentity invertibles have product G (|G|>2), and preserve rank blocks. A gap in any block gives two mutual saturation consequences forcing max(C)=max(B), contradiction. For interval blocks the product is exactly the interval from max(0,a_i+a_j-n) to min(b_i,b_j), so blockwise saturation iff the lower endpoint belongs to the set of starts. Reflection d=n-a gives exact additive closure of a numerical semigroup containing all elements >=n. The inverse map uniquely reconstructs the intervals. Idempotent/nonidempotent rank-one matrices exclude automorphism-orbit equivalence. A standalone checker exhaustively corroborates all small rank partitions through n=9 and GF2 product ranks for n=2,3; these are tests, not a substitute for the general proof.

value.rationale: Theorem classifies a naturally invariant family of lax monoid equivalences in every dimension over every field and supplies a conceptual, bijective translation to numerical-semigroup additive closure. The non-automorphism-orbit result identifies an essential new family outside a standard construction and makes available all known numerical-semigroup enumeration techniques for a matrix-monoid classification. The object and exact invariant are motivated independently of the first nine computed counts; it is neither a bounded toy case nor a mere parameter substitution.
